city.caveat: This is the official city record as kept, without adjustments. It joins several observing sites over the years, and a move, a new instrument or the city growing around a station can shift readings (city growth mostly warms nights); NOAA's adjusted climate datasets correct for these. Treat any single number as approximate.

text.p_yest: The high of 63°F was typical for November 13. The normal high for the date is 66°F, and the record is 80°F (2013). The low of 50°F was the 22nd warmest November 13 low (tied) of 150 since 1877.
text.t_rec: Sacramento is setting record highs far faster than chance
text.p_rec: If Sacramento's climate weren't changing, every year would have the same chance of holding a daily record. Since 2000, Sacramento has set 44 standing record lows, fewer than the 67 that chance alone would give, and 136 record highs, far more than the 67 that chance alone would give. The 2010s hold the most record highs of any decade (55). Sacramento's all-time high is 115°F, on June 15, 1961.
text.t_chg: Sacramento's nights have warmed since 1985. Its days warmed over the long run.
text.p_chg: Across 140 complete years: Sacramento's average low shows no clear change: −0.02°F per decade, a range (−0.06 to +0.03) that includes zero. Sacramento's average high has risen +0.32°F per decade (95% range +0.27 to +0.37), about +4.7°F since 1878. The last 40 years tell a different story: since 1985, lows have risen +0.30°F per decade (95% range +0.03 to +0.57) and highs show no clear change. The full record joins different observing sites over the years, and a move (for example, from the city to a cooler airport) can hide or exaggerate a long-run trend, so the recent decades are the clearer guide here.
text.t_mon: Lows rose in 3 of 12 months; 3 months fell. Highs rose in 11 of 12 months.
text.p_rain: Sacramento's yearly precipitation shows no clear long-term change (−0.07 inches per decade, a range that includes zero). The 1991–2020 normal is 18.0 inches a year. The wettest year was 1884 (34.92 in); the driest, 2013 (5.81 in). Sacramento almost never sees snow (the 1991–2020 average is 0.0 inches a winter), so there's no snowfall chart.
